stem: $\text{PCl}_5$, $\text{PCl}_3$ and $\text{NCl}_3$ are halides of Group 15 elements.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: $\text{PCl}_5$ can be formed from the reaction of phosphorus with chlorine. $\text{PCl}_5$ has a melting point of $161^{\circ}\text{C}$.
parts.text: Write an equation for the formation of $\text{PCl}_5$ from the reaction of phosphorus and chlorine.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State the type of structure and bonding shown by liquid $\text{PCl}_5$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: A small amount of $\text{PCl}_5$ is added to excess water. The $\text{PCl}_5$ reacts vigorously to form a colourless solution.
parts.text: Give **one** other observation you would make when $\text{PCl}_5$ reacts with excess water.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction of $\text{PCl}_5$ with excess water.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Estimate the pH of the resulting solution.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Identify a reagent that could be used in reaction 1.

(c)(iii)
(d)(i)
parts.stem: $\text{NCl}_3$ is a yellow liquid that can be used to bleach flour.
parts.text: Predict the shape of the $\text{NCl}_3$ molecule and the $\text{Cl}-\text{N}-\text{Cl}$ bond angle.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
$\text{NCl}_3$ reacts with water to form $\text{HOCl}$, a weak Brønsted-Lowry acid.

Explain fully what is meant by the term *weak Brønsted-Lowry acid*.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
$\text{NCl}_3(\text{l})$ decomposes according to the equation shown.

$$2\text{NCl}_3(\text{l}) \rightarrow \text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{Cl}_2(\text{g})$$

A sealed container of volume $250\text{ cm}^3$ contains an unreactive gas at a pressure of $1.00 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}$.

$0.241\text{ g}$ of $\text{NCl}_3(\text{l})$ was injected into the sealed container.

The sealed container was heated to make the $\text{NCl}_3(\text{l})$ decompose fully and then cooled to $20^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Calculate the final **total** pressure inside the sealed container at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$ after the $\text{NCl}_3(\text{l})$ has fully decomposed.
